finding: tests/test_signal_search.py:223 The AC3 test does not prove that eight of the nine filters are applied.
rationale: AC3 requires every supplied facet to filter, but the checkpoint's sole filtered query is a nine-way conjunction in which severity="high" alone uniquely selects signal-alpha; signal-beta shares alpha's other eight queried facet values and all projected rows are unreviewed, so ignoring or misrouting any of those eight filters leaves the asserted result unchanged, while producer and projection validation only establish data consistency rather than discriminating test coverage.

evidence.output: Lines 7-15 include AC3: "Filter by detector, group or category, severity, source, table, run, date, and review state when supplied."

The fixture gives signal-alpha severity high and signal-beta severity low, but both have detector numeric.zscore_outliers, category outlier, source payments, TABLE_ALPHA, run-alpha, date 2026-08-21, group numeric, and review_state unreviewed; signal-gamma differs but has severity medium. Lines 223-232 submit all nine filters together, line 239 only asserts ["signal-alpha"], and source inspection found this is the only filters= call in the test file. Therefore severity alone produces the expected assertion even if the other eight filters are ignored.

search.py lines 23-32 map nine public filter keys and lines 68-71 pass all supplied mappings to read_rows; _signal_projection.py lines 149-150 build conjunctive SQL, lines 233-243 project the nine corresponding facet values, and line 229 hard-codes current review_state to unreviewed. This shows the implementation is presently wired, but supplies no upstream guard that would make a missing individual-filter regression fail the AC3 test.
